intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that monilethrix-2 (MNLIX2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding the type II hair cortex keratin hHb1 (KRT81; 602153) on chromosome 12q13.

checks.claim: Monilethrix-2 (MNLIX2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KRT81 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In the second family, we identified in affected individuals a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1
checks.explanation: The abstract links an hHb1 mutation to monilethrix in a dominant family. It does not explicitly call the hHb1 mutation heterozygous; that word is used only for the earlier hHb6 mutations.

checks.claim: KRT81 encodes the type II hair cortex keratin hHb1.
checks.evidence_quote: A new mutation in the type II hair cortex keratin hHb1 involved in the inherited hair disorder monilethrix.
checks.explanation: The paper describes hHb1 as a type II hair cortex keratin. KRT81 is its standard symbol.

checks.claim: The KRT81 gene is located on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Several cases of monilethrix have been linked to the type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13
checks.explanation: The location is standard nomenclature, consistent with hHb1 being a type II hair keratin in the 12q13 cluster.

paragraphs.text: Monilethrix is an inherited hair shaft disorder. The hair is beaded: elliptical nodes alternate with narrow, constricted internodes, and the hair breaks easily at the internodes. The result is short, sparse, brittle hair, mainly on the scalp, often with keratotic follicular papules (keratosis pilaris), especially on the occiput and nape. The disorder usually appears in early childhood after the lanugo hair is shed. Severity varies, even within a family.

checks.claim: Monilethrix is an inherited hair shaft disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Monilethrix is a rare dominant hair disease characterized by beaded or moniliform hair which results from the periodic thinning of the hair shaft
checks.explanation: The title calls it an 'inherited hair disorder', and the abstract describes the hair shaft involvement.

checks.claim: In monilethrix, the hair is beaded, with elliptical nodes alternating with narrow, constricted internodes.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by beaded or moniliform hair which results from the periodic thinning of the hair shaft
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions beading and periodic thinning but not elliptical nodes alternating with internodes.

checks.claim: In monilethrix, the hair breaks easily at the internodes.
checks.evidence_quote: shows a high propensity to excess weathering and fracturing
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions fracturing but does not say where along the shaft the hair breaks (the internodes).

checks.claim: Monilethrix results in short, sparse, brittle hair, mainly on the scalp.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not describe short, sparse, brittle scalp hair.

checks.claim: Monilethrix is often accompanied by keratotic follicular papules (keratosis pilaris), especially on the occiput and nape.
checks.evidence_quote: one with pronounced dystrophic alopecia, follicular keratosis, and clear-cut moniliform hair
checks.explanation: Follicular keratosis is noted in one patient; the abstract does not say it is frequent or give the occiput/nape location.

checks.claim: Monilethrix usually appears in early childhood after the lanugo hair is shed.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract gives no age of onset and does not mention lanugo hair.

checks.claim: The severity of monilethrix varies, even within a family.
checks.evidence_quote: Family members bearing the hHb1 Glu402Lys mutation exhibit a particularly variable disease phenotype.
checks.explanation: Variable severity within a single family is described.

paragraphs.text: Monilethrix caused by KRT81 mutation is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait with variable expressivity.

checks.claim: Monilethrix caused by KRT81 mutation is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: Monilethrix is a rare human hair disorder with autosomal dominant transmission that can be caused by mutations in hair keratins.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant transmission of keratin-related monilethrix, including hHb1, is stated.

checks.claim: Monilethrix caused by KRT81 mutation shows variable expressivity.
checks.evidence_quote: Family members bearing the hHb1 Glu402Lys mutation exhibit a particularly variable disease phenotype.
checks.explanation: The family with the hHb1 mutation shows variable expressivity.

paragraphs.text: Linkage studies in families with autosomal dominant monilethrix mapped the disorder to the type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13, which contains KRT81.

checks.claim: Linkage studies in families with autosomal dominant monilethrix mapped the disorder to the type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Several cases of monilethrix have been linked to the type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13
checks.explanation: The abstract states this linkage directly.

checks.claim: The type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13 contains KRT81.
checks.evidence_quote: suggesting that this site represents a mutational hotspot in these highly related type II hair keratins
checks.explanation: The abstract calls hHb1 a type II hair keratin but does not explicitly place it in the 12q13 cluster.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant monilethrix is genetically heterogeneous. It can be caused by mutations in the type II hair cortex keratin genes KRT86 (hHb6), KRT81 (hHb1) and KRT83 (hHb3), which are clustered on chromosome 12q13. A clinically similar autosomal recessive monilethrix-like hypotrichosis is caused by mutation in the desmoglein-4 gene (DSG4).

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant monilethrix is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: In the second family, we identified in affected individuals a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1
checks.explanation: Mutations in two different genes (hHb6 and hHb1) cause dominant monilethrix, so the disorder is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant monilethrix can be caused by mutations in the type II hair cortex keratin genes KRT86 (hHb6), KRT81 (hHb1), and KRT83 (hHb3).
checks.evidence_quote: Affected members of one family and the single patient exhibited the prevalent hHb6 Glu 410 Lys mutation. In the second family, we identified in affected individuals a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1
checks.explanation: The abstract supports hHb6 and hHb1. It does not mention KRT83 (hHb3).

checks.claim: The KRT86, KRT81, and KRT83 genes are clustered on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Several cases of monilethrix have been linked to the type II keratin gene cluster on chromosome 12q13
checks.explanation: The abstract names the 12q13 cluster but does not mention KRT83 or explicitly place these genes in it.

checks.claim: A clinically similar autosomal recessive monilethrix-like hypotrichosis is caused by mutation in the desmoglein-4 gene (DSG4).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention DSG4 or a recessive form.

paragraphs.text: Winter et al. (1997) found a heterozygous mutation in the helix termination motif of the hair cortex keratin hHb1 (KRT81) in a patient with monilethrix. This showed that monilethrix can be caused by mutations in hHb1 as well as in hHb6 (KRT86). The mutation changed a conserved glutamic acid residue in the highly conserved helix termination motif of the rod domain, the same region that is affected in hHb6-associated monilethrix.

checks.claim: Winter et al. (1997) found a heterozygous mutation in the helix termination motif of the hair cortex keratin hHb1 (KRT81) in a patient with monilethrix.
checks.evidence_quote: In the second family, we identified in affected individuals a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1
checks.explanation: The hHb1 mutation was found in affected members of a family, not in a single patient. The single patient had the hHb6 Glu410Lys mutation. The abstract also does not call the hHb1 mutation heterozygous.

checks.claim: The finding of a KRT81 mutation in a patient with monilethrix showed that monilethrix can be caused by mutations in hHb1 (KRT81) as well as in hHb6 (KRT86).
checks.evidence_quote: suggesting that this site represents a mutational hotspot in these highly related type II hair keratins
checks.explanation: The paper found monilethrix mutations in both hHb6 and hHb1.

checks.claim: The KRT81 mutation found in a monilethrix patient by Winter et al. (1997) changed a conserved glutamic acid residue in the highly conserved helix termination motif of the hHb1 rod domain.
checks.evidence_quote: a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1
checks.explanation: The abstract supports a change at a glutamic acid residue that corresponds to the hHb6 site in the helix termination motif. It does not mention the rod domain, and the variant (Glu403Lys) is not specified in the claim.

checks.claim: The helix termination motif affected by the KRT81 mutation in monilethrix is the same region affected in hHb6 (KRT86)-associated monilethrix.
checks.evidence_quote: a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1, suggesting that this site represents a mutational hotspot
checks.explanation: The residue corresponds to the hHb6 Glu410 site in the helix termination motif. That it lies in the same motif is implied by 'corresponding' rather than stated outright.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Follicular keratotic papules, especially occiput and nape
Beaded hair shafts (moniliform hair) with periodic nodes and internodes
